cards.explanation: The answer is he bows his knees. Paul says, "…I bow my knees before the Father…" (Ephesians 3:14), and he calls himself an ambassador in chains (Ephesians 6:20) and the prisoner of Christ Jesus (Ephesians 3:1). Whatever his chains were doing, his knees were still free to bow. I think a lot of us could learn from a man who prays from right where he is.

The first thing Paul asks is that the Father strengthen them with power. He asks that "…He may strengthen you with power through His Spirit in your inner being…" (Ephesians 3:16). Notice he starts with strength, not a to-do list. I think a prisoner like Paul (Ephesians 3:1) knows how much a person needs it.

The power comes through His Spirit. Paul says the strength comes "…through His Spirit in your inner being…" (Ephesians 3:16). The Spirit is the Holy Spirit, one of the three I believe in. The power comes through Him.

The answer is that Christ may dwell in their hearts. Paul prays for strength "…so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith." (Ephesians 3:17). Dwell means to settle in and stay. That's a lot better than a visit, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says they'll have power, "…together with all the saints, to comprehend the length and width and height and depth" (Ephesians 3:18). It's a shared grasp, friends. The saints do this one side by side, not each one alone.

The word is love. Paul says "the length and width and height and depth of the love of Christ" (Ephesians 3:18-19). Four directions, and every one of them is love. I'd need a bigger cookie box to measure that.

It means the love of Christ is bigger than our minds can hold. Paul calls it "…this love that surpasses knowledge…" (Ephesians 3:19). Surpasses means it goes beyond what we can wrap our heads around. And he still prays that we'd know it. Quite a thing, friends.

God is able to do immeasurably more. Paul says God "…is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine…" (Ephesians 3:20). Immeasurably means you can't get out a ruler. Whatever you're picturing, friends, He's able to go past it.

Paul says the glory is in the church and in Christ Jesus. He writes, "…to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus…" (Ephesians 3:21). He gives glory to God in the church and in Christ Jesus, side by side. That's a whole lot of glory going to the right Person.
The answer is False. Paul says, "…throughout all generations, forever and ever." (Ephesians 3:21). It's not just his own time, friends. Every generation gets to join in, and that includes ours.
